uuid@9.0.1 is vulnerable to CVE-2026-41907 (MEDIUM severity, silent partial writes into caller-provided buffers in v3/v5/v6 functions). The fix is available in uuid@11.1.1. However, upgrading from uuid@9.x to uuid@11.x is a major version jump that would require significant testing and may introduce breaking changes in transitive dependencies. The vulnerability affects applications that pass external buffers to uuid v3/v5/v6 functions with attacker-controlled offsets or undersized buffers; langfuse's typical usage does not expose this attack surface.

webpack is a build-time tool; the runtime image only executes the Next.js standalone server bundle and never invokes webpack itself. The SSRF vulnerability requires running webpack's dev/build server, which the production image does not. The vulnerable code paths are not reachable through the entrypoint server.js.

Langfuse 2.x is end-of-life upstream (last release v2.95.12 on 2025-11-18; no further releases). Next.js is bumped to 14.2.35 (latest 14.x); the upstream fix only exists in the 15.x major line which DHI v2 cannot adopt without breaking compatibility with the langfuse 2.x bundle. Customers requiring active CVE remediation should adopt the langfuse 3.x DHI variant (Next 16); this v2 image is published for migration compatibility only.

False positive. CVE-2026-22184 affects the untgz utility that is part of zlib source code, but Debian zlib packages (zlib1g and zlib1g-dev) do not ship the untgz utility by default. For Debian Trixie (and other versions), zlib comes from zlib1g (binaries) and does not include the untgz binary. The vulnerability scanner incorrectly flags zlib packages as vulnerable when the untgz utility is not actually present in the installed packages.
